content:
incident-bot: ALERT: auth-service anomaly detected. unusual pattern: repeated 403/401 from refresh-token endpoint and surge of token-introspect calls. Suspected leaked credentials or scraping. Paging Priya (oncall) and Theo (security). Link: https://grafana.example.com/d/auth/refresh-spike

Priya (oncall): I'm on it. quick read: are we seeing any customer-facing 5xx?

Omar (SRE): traffic spike started 2026-03-16T01:12:00Z. sample logs:
```
2026-03-16T01:12:03Z auth-svc WARN refresh-loop ip=45.33.77.12 client=svc-replicate attempts=412 status=401
2026-03-16T01:12:05Z auth-svc ERROR token-reuse-detected uid=svc-replicate token_hash=sha256:... source_ip=45.33.77.12
```
No systemic 5xx but elevated 429/401 on upload routes. Mei, any support tickets?

Mei (support): yes, two tickets from orbit-markets and lilt-ai reporting failed background syncs and 401s. Escalated to me. I'll hold messaging until we have a mitigation summary.

Theo (security): acknowledging. I'll start IOCs and look for recent changes that could've exposed tokens. Check: did any deploys last 24h change logging level?

Priya (oncall): checking deploy history... there was a debug flag flip in deploy-agent at 2026-03-15T22:40Z for a staging patch that accidentally targeted prod pipeline. Could be noisy logs. Omar, can you confirm whether any tokens were logged?

Omar (SRE): running grep across logs for token-looking strings. Found a few entries in `s3://prod-logs/deploy-agent/2026-03-15/` with short-lived access tokens appended to debug messages. That explains scraping.

Theo (security): confirmed probable leak. Immediate actions: 1) revoke active tokens for svc-replicate and any clients that used that deploy-agent role 2) rotate IAM keys used by deploy-agent 3) block known abusive IPs 45.33.77.12/32 and 45.33.77.13/32 4) redact S3 objects containing tokens and lock down bucket ACLs.

Priya (oncall): executing revocation for session tokens now: `POST /admin/revoke?service=svc-replicate` -> 200. Applying WAF bans.

Priya (oncall): WAF commands:
```
wafctl ban add 45.33.77.12/32 --reason "auth abuse"
wafctl ban add 45.33.77.13/32 --reason "auth abuse"
```

Omar (SRE): rotating deploy-agent IAM keys and updating secrets manager. Steps run:
```
# create new access key
aws iam create-access-key --user deploy-agent-prod
# update sm
aws secretsmanager put-secret-value --secret-id /prod/deploy-agent/key --secret-string "<new>"
# restart deploy-agent pods to pick up creds
kubectl rollout restart deployment/deploy-agent -n infra
```

Mei (support): any ETA before clients stop seeing 401s?

Priya (oncall): expect transient auth failures for up to 20 minutes while cached tokens expire and clients rotate. We're also restarting a couple of auth caches to accelerate flush.

Theo (security): I'm copying artifacts to secure forensic bucket and kicking off a search for lateral access. Also notifying legal/compliance per breach policy. compliance-bot: please log incident.

compliance-bot: Incident recorded INC-2026-0556. Notifying privacy team. Recommend hold on public customer notice until we confirm scope.

Omar (SRE): rolling restart of auth pods: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/auth-service -n prod --timeout=5m`. Cache flush initiated.

Priya (oncall): monitoring: auth 401 rate peaked at 14% between 01:12-01:20 UTC; now down to ~2.1% after revokes and restarts. Introspect call rate reduced by 85% after WAF bans.

Mei (support): prepping customer webhook to affected tenants. Draft message for review:
"We detected unusual authentication attempts affecting background syncs for some customers. We have revoked affected service sessions, applied blocks, rotated deploy-agent credentials, and are reviewing logs for exposure. You may experience up to 20 minutes of transient 401 errors while systems recover. If issues persist, please reply and we will prioritize your tenant."

Priya (oncall): looks good. Approve sending to orbit-markets, lilt-ai, and any tenant that used svc-replicate in last 48h.

Theo (security): recommendation: delete leaked objects from S3 (after copying to secure bucket for forensics) and tighten deploy pipeline permissions. Add token-detection linter pre-commit for deploy-agent logging.

Omar (SRE): redaction plan: copy and scrub logs, then rewrite bucket with restricted ACLs. Command queued:
```
aws s3 cp s3://prod-logs/deploy-agent/2026-03-15/ ./tmp && python redact_tokens.py ./tmp && aws s3 sync ./tmp s3://prod-logs/deploy-agent/2026-03-15/ --acl private
```

Priya (oncall): setting alert: token-reuse detections > 3/min to page security. Also lowering introspect-rate-threshold for high-sensitivity clients.

compliance-bot: please retain all artifacts for 120 days per policy. Legal has been CC'd for potential disclosure obligations.

Mei (support): messages sent to customers; some replied acknowledging and asking for timeline — I'll give them ETA of 20 minutes and offer expedited troubleshooting if they still see errors.

Theo (security): marking containment complete. Moving to investigation: check for any pulling of internal buckets from suspicious IPs, check for reuse of leaked tokens against other services.

Omar (SRE): systems stable. No further abusive IPs detected after bans. Auth error rate steady below 1.5%.

Priya (oncall): handing off to night crew. Handoff notes: watch auth-401 > 2% or any repeated token-reuse alerts. If tokens reappear in logs, page security immediately.

incident-bot: Status updated -> mitigated. Severity P1 -> PIR required. Thread archived.
